title: Discovery of highly potent marine-derived compound Penicolinate H reveals SREBP-1 mediated lipogenesis as a druggable vulnerability in gastric cancer.
authors: Chen, Jianjiao; Cui, Haishan; Wang, Xiaolu; Zeng, Yechun; Pan, Dongyue; Chen, Jun; Zhang, Zhenhua; An, Yana; Gu, Zhanfeng; Cai, Guodi; Wang, Hong; Yu, Mengya; Yang, Bin; Zhou, Shengning; Tan, Jianan; Liu, Lan; Wang, Junjian; Li, Jing; Han, Fanghai
one_liner_zh: 该文研究海洋来源化合物Penicolinate H通过抑制SREBP-1介导的脂质合成治疗胃癌，属于药物靶点与代谢机制研究，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或AI/物理模拟建模方法。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Gastric cancer (GC) is a highly aggressive and fatal disease, with limited treatment options. Altered cellular lipid metabolism is a hallmark of cancer that contributes to GC progression. However, the determinants of lipid metabolism in GC and new agents that target lipid metabolic pathways are poorly defined. The aim of this study was to identify potentially effective lead anti-GC compounds by developing and exploring natural marine products. Furthermore, we sought to uncover viable therapeutic targets for GC through the underlying mechanisms of action of the compounds as an anticancer agent. METHODS: The chemical structures of the metabolites produced by the crinoid-derived fungus Penicillium brocae SYSU-CJ17 were elucidated using advanced spectroscopic techniques. These metabolites were screened for their growth-inhibitory effects on GC cell lines. Among them, Penicolinate H (Pen-H) demonstrated the most significant anti-cancer activity. High-throughput RNA sequencing of Pen-H-treated GC samples revealed differentially expressed genes, and transcriptomic data integrated with bioinformatics analyses highlighted the potential pathways and target genes through which Pen-H might exert its anti-cancer effects. Further investigations, including rescue experiments, endogenous affinity pull-down assays, cellular thermal shift assays (CETSA), surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assays, molecular docking, and in vitro analyses, confirmed the interaction between Pen-H and SREBP-1. The feasibility of SREBP-1 as a therapeutic target for GC is supported by single-cell transcriptome analysis, bioinformatics evaluation of GC patient data, and in vitro studies. Additionally, the chemosensitization effect of Pen-H was confirmed by in vivo and in vitro experiments. RESULTS: Our findings reveal a novel marine-derived compound, Pen-H, which inhibits GC growth and metastasis both in vitro and in vivo by suppressing SREBP-1 mediated lipogenesis. Bioinformatic analysis indicated that SREBP-1 was highly expressed in GC tissues, and high SREBP-1 transcript levels were negatively correlated with prognosis in GC patients. SREBP-1 depletion significantly inhibits the proliferation, migration, and invasion of GC cells. Mechanistic studies have revealed that targeting SREBP-1 by Pen-H significantly reduces de novo fatty acid synthesis and that the anti-GC efficacy of Pen-H is SREBP-1 dependent. Moreover, combination treatment with Pen-H and 5-fluorouracil (5-Fu) resulted in enhanced inhibition of cell proliferation and tumor growth compared to monotherapy. CONCLUSION: Taken together, these findings highlight that SREBP-1 is an effective therapeutic target in GC and that Pen-H is a promising SREBP-1 inhibitor and a candidate for GC treatment.
abstract_zh: 背景：胃癌（GC）是一种高度侵袭性和致命性疾病，治疗选择有限。细胞脂质代谢的改变是癌症的一个标志，有助于胃癌的进展。然而，胃癌中脂质代谢的决定因素以及靶向脂质代谢途径的新型药物尚不明确。本研究旨在通过开发和探索天然海洋产物，识别潜在有效的抗胃癌先导化合物。此外，我们试图通过化合物作为抗癌药物的作用机制，揭示胃癌可行的治疗靶点。方法：利用先进的光谱技术阐明了由海百合来源真菌Penicillium brocae SYSU-CJ17产生的代谢产物的化学结构。筛选了这些代谢产物对胃癌细胞系的生长抑制作用。其中，Penicolinate H（Pen-H）表现出最显著的抗癌活性。对Pen-H处理的胃癌样本进行高通量RNA测序，揭示了差异表达基因，转录组数据与生物信息学分析相结合，突出了Pen-H可能发挥其抗癌作用的潜在途径和靶基因。进一步的研究，包括拯救实验、内源性亲和拉下实验、细胞热位移分析（CETSA）、表面等离子体共振（SPR）实验、分子对接和体外分析，确认了Pen-H与SREBP-1之间的相互作用。SREBP-1作为胃癌治疗靶点的可行性得到了单细胞转录组分析、胃癌患者数据的生物信息学评估以及体外研究的支持。此外，Pen-H的化学增敏作用通过体内和体外实验得到确认。结果：我们的发现揭示了一种新型海洋来源化合物Pen-H，它通过抑制SREBP-1介导的脂质生成，在体外和体内抑制胃癌的生长和转移。生物信息学分析表明，SREBP-1在胃癌组织中高表达，且高SREBP-1转录水平与胃癌患者的预后呈负相关。SREBP-1的缺失显著抑制胃癌细胞的增殖、迁移和侵袭。机制研究表明，Pen-H靶向SREBP-1显著减少从头脂肪酸合成，且Pen-H的抗胃癌功效依赖于SREBP-1。此外，与单一疗法相比，Pen-H和5-氟尿嘧啶（5-Fu）的联合治疗导致细胞增殖和肿瘤生长的抑制增强。结论：综合来看，这些发现强调SREBP-1是胃癌的有效治疗靶点，Pen-H是一种有前景的SREBP-1抑制剂，并可作为胃癌治疗的候选药物。
